target_reference_entry: C. Wang et al., “Thru-the-wall eavesdropping on loudspeakers via RFID by capturing sub-mm level vibration,” Proc. ACM Interact., Mobile, Wearable Ubiquitous Technol., vol. 5, no. 4, pp. 1–25, 2021.
paper_level_summary_zh: 该论文将目标文献作为RFID振动感知的代表性相关工作在引言中提及，并指出其波长较长导致对小位移检测能力受限。正文中未直接引用目标文献的结论或方法，属于一般性对比引用。

evidences.evidence_quote: RFID-based solutions [11], [12], which are long-wavelength wireless systems, have a restricted sensitivity to vibrations.
evidences.evidence_context: Although current RF solutions offer benefits, they are still subject to certain limitations. RFID-based solutions [11], [12], which are long-wavelength wireless systems, have a restricted sensitivity to vibrations. The spatial resolution of Wi-Fi [13] is inadequate for achieving accurate spatial differentiation and measuring vibrations at multiple points.

evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 该引用出现在对现有RF方案局限性的概述中，将[11]等RFID方案归为长波长系统，限制了对振动的敏感性。这是对RFID类方案的普遍批评，未单独描述目标论文的具体贡献，且引用为分组引用([11],[12])，未明确锚定目标论文的特性。
